title: DiffCCD: Differentiable Concurrent Clock and Data Optimization
problem: Post-CTS timing optimization must address clock skew and data path delays while respecting physical implementation constraints. Traditional methods handle these optimizations separately, limiting effectiveness in timing closure for advanced nodes.
motivation: Achieving timing closure on modern VLSI designs requires joint optimization of clock skew and data delays with physical constraints, as clock skew significantly impacts circuit timing performance.
method: DiffCCD formulates concurrent clock and data optimization as a GPU-accelerated differentiable optimization problem. The approach includes: (1) smooth differentiable formulation for CCD optimization with gradient calibration mechanism; (2) ADMM-based problem decomposition into manageable subproblems; (3) implementation as buffer sizing in clock network and placement refinement, balancing timing optimization with physical constraints.
key_novelty: First differentiable framework to jointly optimize clock skew and data path delays during post-CTS timing closure with physical constraint awareness.
contributions: Differentiable formulation of concurrent clock and data optimization with calibrated gradient computation
ADMM-based decomposition strategy balancing timing optimization with physical implementation constraints
GPU-accelerated implementation demonstrating 22.4% average WNS improvement and 45.0% TNS improvement
9.434× runtime speedup on industrial open-source benchmarks

metrics.other: timing closure enhancement for VLSI design

baselines: baseline approach in open-source physical design tool
limitations: Evaluation limited to open-source benchmarks; applicability to proprietary industrial designs and very advanced technology nodes (3nm and below) is not discussed.
